subtopics.title: India's Partnerships: Vietnam, New Zealand and SAARC
subtopics.summary: India and Vietnam raised their ties to an enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership after a state visit by To Lam, with a target of USD 25 billion bilateral trade by 2030. India and New Zealand signed a free trade agreement that eliminates duties on Indian exports to New Zealand. The SAARC currency swap framework, launched by the RBI in 2012, offers short-term liquidity support to member nations.
facts: India and Vietnam elevated ties to an enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership after a state visit by To Lam
Target: USD 25 billion bilateral trade by 2030
Vietnam formally joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative
Joint Vision Statement for 2030 seeks deeper defence cooperation and joint development of advanced defence platforms
India extended a USD 500 million defence line of credit to Vietnam
India-New Zealand FTA eliminates duties on Indian exports to New Zealand (100% duty elimination)
India gives access to 70.03% of tariff lines and keeps 29.97% under exclusion
New Zealand to invest USD 20 billion over 15 years
SAARC currency swap: central banks exchange domestic currencies at a predetermined rate and reverse the swap at the same rate
SAARC swap tenure is 3 months, extendable twice; launched by RBI in 2012

subtopics.title: ASEAN: Structure, Principles and Forums
subtopics.summary: ASEAN was formed on 8 August 1967 and is headquartered in Jakarta, with 11 members now including Timor-Leste. It works on three principles: non-interference, consensual decision-making and centrality in regional matters, and its Charter took effect in 2008. The group runs several forums and economic pacts, and India's Act East Policy places ASEAN at the centre of its Indo-Pacific vision.
facts: Formed on 8 August 1967 at Bangkok, Thailand; headquarters in Jakarta, Indonesia
11 members, including Timor-Leste (2025)
Core aims: accelerate economic and social progress, promote regional peace and stability, foster collaboration, cooperate with global organisations
Principles: non-interference in internal affairs, consensual decision-making, and maintaining centrality in regional matters
ASEAN Charter took effect on 15 December 2008; it is legally binding and registered with the UN Secretariat
East Asia Summit created in 2005 as a leaders-level forum with a varied agenda
ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) established in 1992 to create a single market
ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) established in 1994 for political and security dialogue
ASEAN Economic Community formed in 2015 to facilitate free flow of goods, services, investments, capital and labour
RCEP concluded in 2019, covering 30% of the world's population

subtopics.title: Global Issues: Thucydides Trap, Ebola and Ecocide
subtopics.summary: The Thucydides Trap describes the heightened risk of conflict when a rising power challenges an established power, and it is often applied to China and the United States. WHO declared an Ebola outbreak in DR Congo a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, linked to the Bundibugyo strain. Ecocide refers to unlawful or reckless acts that cause severe environmental damage, and it is not currently recognised under the Rome Statute.
facts: The Thucydides Trap idea originates from Thucydides' account of the Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta
Core argument: growth of Athenian power and the fear it caused in Sparta made conflict increasingly inevitable
The trap describes a heightened risk of conflict when a rising power challenges an established power
Critics argue the idea oversimplifies by implying conflict is unavoidable; diplomacy and economic interdependence can prevent escalation
WHO declared the DR Congo Ebola outbreak a PHEIC, linked to the Bundibugyo strain in the Ituri region
Under the IHR 2005, a PHEIC is a public health risk of international disease spread requiring coordinated global response
Ebola is a zoonotic, severe and fatal viral disease, first identified in 1976
Ecocide: unlawful or reckless acts committed knowing they are likely to cause severe, widespread or long-term environmental damage
Ecocide is not currently recognised under the Rome Statute; India has not signed the Rome Statute and is not bound by ICC jurisdiction
Recognised international crimes under the Rome Statute: genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and crime of aggression

subtopics.title: Governance, Citizenship and Parliament
subtopics.summary: Draft Citizenship Rules amendments tighten declaration and passport-surrender norms for applicants from Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh, and India does not allow dual citizenship. A privilege notice moved in Rajya Sabha shows how MPs can allege a breach of parliamentary privilege. The Model Code of Conduct regulates elections, and the Supreme Court's One Case One Data initiative aims to integrate court data.
facts: Citizenship is covered under Part II (Articles 5 to 11) of the Constitution and is a Union List subject
India does not allow dual citizenship; acquiring foreign citizenship leads to automatic termination of Indian citizenship
Applicants must declare whether they hold a valid or expired passport from Pakistan, Afghanistan or Bangladesh
Under the draft rules, a foreign passport must be surrendered within 15 days
Citizenship Act, 1955 lists five modes of acquisition: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory
A privilege notice is a formal mechanism to allege breach of parliamentary privilege or contempt of the House; it is derived from Article 105
Privilege notices are submitted under Lok Sabha Rule 222 or Rajya Sabha Rule 187; the Speaker or Chairman decides whether to allow discussion or refer it to the Privileges Committee
Model Code of Conduct: non-statutory guidelines issued by the Election Commission to ensure a free, fair and level-playing field, with no unfair advantage to the ruling party
One Case One Data integrates case data from the Supreme Court, High Courts, district courts and taluka courts into one platform; Su Sahay is an AI chatbot on the Supreme Court website

subtopics.title: Economy, Agriculture and Employment
subtopics.summary: The RBI's Economic Capital Framework governs how it provides for risks and transfers surplus to the government, and the RBI Board approved a record transfer for FY 2025-26. The Index of Eight Core Industries and the Manufacturing PMI track industrial activity, with the PMI at 54.7 in April 2026. The Mission for Cotton Productivity aims at self-sufficiency in cotton by 2030-31, and the Centre raised the sugarcane Fair and Remunerative Price for the 2026-27 season.
facts: Economic Capital Framework (introduced in 2019) governs how the RBI provides for financial risks and transfers surplus to the Government of India
Surplus is transferred to the government only after Contingency Risk Buffer targets are met
RBI Board approved a record 2.86 lakh crore surplus transfer for FY 2025-26
Section 47 of the RBI Act, 1934 mandates that RBI profits be sent to the Centre
RBI surplus transfer typically averages around 0.5% of GDP
Eight core industries: coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity (base year 2011-12)
Index of Eight Core Industries grew 1.7% in April 2026; core industries carry a 40.27% weight in the Index of Industrial Production
Manufacturing PMI rose to 54.7 in April 2026; a PMI above 50 signals expansion, compiled by S&P Global
Mission for Cotton Productivity (Kapas Kanti), 2026-27 to 2030-31, aims to make India self-sufficient in cotton
Bt cotton is the only GM crop approved by GEAC for commercial cultivation in India

quizzes.passage:
India and Vietnam have raised their bilateral ties to an enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, a formal upgrade that followed a state visit by a Vietnamese leader. The two countries have also agreed on a trade goal and plan deeper defence cooperation, including joint development of advanced defence platforms, which is set out in a Joint Vision Statement. Vietnam has formally joined an Indo-Pacific initiative that India supports, and the relationship is linked to India's wider engagement with Southeast Asia.

India has also signed a free trade agreement with New Zealand. A free trade agreement is a pact between countries to reduce or eliminate customs duties and liberalise trade in services, and it also ensures investment protection and safeguards for intellectual property rights. Sensitive sectors such as dairy and agriculture are kept outside the deal to protect domestic producers, and the two countries have agreed to mutually recognise organic certification standards.

In South Asia, the SAARC currency swap framework is a bilateral arrangement between central banks. Members exchange domestic currencies at a predetermined rate and reverse the exchange at a future date. The framework provides short-term liquidity support to member nations, helps them during balance of payments crises, reduces dependence on external borrowing and strengthens regional financial stability.

India and Vietnam have agreed to lift their relationship to a higher strategic level after a state visit by a Vietnamese leader. The two countries have set a trade target for 2030 and plan closer defence ties, including work on advanced defence platforms. Vietnam has also formally joined an Indo-Pacific initiative that India promotes. Military exercises between the two countries also take place.

India has signed a free trade agreement with New Zealand. Such an agreement is a pact between countries that reduces customs duties and liberalises trade, and it provides investment protection and safeguards for intellectual property. In this deal India keeps some sensitive sectors outside its concessions to protect domestic producers, while New Zealand has also made an investment commitment. The SAARC currency swap framework is a bilateral arrangement between central banks. Members exchange domestic currencies at a predetermined rate and reverse the exchange later, which gives short-term liquidity support. The arrangement also aims to reduce dependence on external borrowing, promote the use of the Indian rupee internationally and strengthen regional financial stability. Such a framework is designed to help member nations in times of short-term financial need.

quizzes.passage:
The Thucydides Trap is a phrase used in international relations to describe the danger of conflict when a rising power challenges a power that is already dominant. The idea comes from the writings of Thucydides, who analysed a long war between two rival powers. Its core idea is that fear and rivalry between powers can make a clash more likely, and the concept is often discussed in relation to a rising power and an existing global power. Critics argue that the idea oversimplifies politics by suggesting conflict is unavoidable, while others stress that diplomacy and economic links can prevent escalation.

The World Health Organization has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo to be a serious international health emergency. Under the International Health Regulations, such a declaration applies when a health risk could spread across borders and needs a coordinated response. Ebola is a severe viral disease that can affect humans and primates.

Ecocide refers to unlawful or reckless acts that cause severe, widespread or long-term environmental damage, carried out with knowledge that such damage is likely. The idea has gained legal attention, and several countries have written it into their own laws, which is one reason it is discussed in environmental debates.

Reason (R): Ebola was first identified in 1976.

quizzes.passage:
A rising power that challenges an established power can end up in conflict, a pattern that a historian's account of an old war helped to describe. Its core idea is that fear and rivalry between powers can make a clash more likely. Modern analysts apply this idea to today's great-power rivalries, though critics stress that it can make war seem more inevitable than it is. Diplomacy, trade ties and international institutions are often cited as ways to reduce the risk of confrontation.

Health authorities have also been busy. The World Health Organization has issued a formal emergency declaration over an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Such a declaration is used when a health risk could spread across borders and needs a coordinated global response. Ebola is a severe and fatal viral disease that can affect humans and primates. The disease was formerly known as Ebola haemorrhagic fever.

Environmental harm is drawing legal attention too. Acts that cause severe, widespread or long-term damage to nature, when committed knowingly or recklessly, are described as ecocide. Examples often cited include the Deepwater Horizon oil spill and large-scale deforestation in the Amazon. Several countries have written this idea into their own laws.

quizzes.passage:
Citizenship and parliamentary conduct are both constitutional matters. The Centre has notified draft amendments to the Citizenship Rules that tighten the rules for applicants with links to certain neighbouring countries. Such applicants must declare the passports they hold or have held, and they must give full passport details for verification. The rules sit within the constitutional framework for citizenship, which is a subject placed on the Union List.

Members of Parliament have their own tools for raising concerns. A privilege notice is a formal way for a member to allege a breach of parliamentary privilege or contempt of the House. The notice is submitted under the rules of the House concerned, and the presiding officer then decides whether it can be discussed or sent to a committee. The aim is to protect the dignity and independence of Parliament.

Elections in India follow a code issued by the Election Commission. The code is a set of guidelines and not a law, and it applies to political parties, candidates and the government in power. Its purpose is to ensure a free and fair contest. The Supreme Court has also introduced digital tools, including an online chatbot on its website that helps litigants find procedural information.

quizzes.passage:
Citizenship is a subject that the Constitution places under the Union, and the Citizenship Act sets out how citizenship can be acquired and lost. Under the latest draft changes, applicants who have held passports from certain neighbouring countries must declare them, and a foreign passport must be surrendered within a set period after citizenship is granted. Applicants must also provide full passport details so that the authorities can verify them.

Parliament also guards its own dignity. A member who believes a minister or an outside body has breached parliamentary privilege can raise the matter through a formal privilege notice, a mechanism that is grounded in the Constitution. Such a notice can be raised against a minister, a member or an outside individual or institution. The presiding officer then decides whether the House should discuss the matter or refer it to a privileges committee. The aim is to protect the authority and independence of Parliament.

Public life has its own rules during elections. The Election Commission issues guidelines so that contests are free and fair, and these guidelines stop the ruling party from gaining an unfair advantage. Meanwhile the Supreme Court is bringing case records from several levels of courts into one digital platform, called One Case One Data.
